target: Jangan sampai paspor kamu ketinggalan di taksi.
english: Don't let your passport get left behind in the taxi.
tip: Ke-...-an marks accidents: tinggal = stay behind, ketinggalan = got left behind – nobody did it on purpose. Same move in ketiduran (accidentally fell asleep).

target: Ini boarding pass Anda, pesawat berangkat dari pintu lima.
english: Here is your boarding pass; the plane departs from gate five.
tip: boarding pass stays English at Indonesian airports; pintu = gate here.

target: Antrean di imigrasi panjang sekali pagi ini.
english: The line at immigration is very long this morning.
tip: The -an ending turns an action into its thing: antre = to queue up, antrean = the line itself. Same trick in makan – makanan (food), minum – minuman (drink).

target: Penerbangan kami ditunda satu jam karena hujan deras.
english: Our flight is delayed one hour because of heavy rain.
tip: di- flips who does it: menunda = postpone, ditunda = postponed: penerbangan ditunda = the flight is delayed.

target: Penerbangan pengganti baru ada besok pagi jam enam.
english: The replacement flight is only available tomorrow morning at six.
tip: baru means new, but before a verb it means only just or not until: penerbangan pengganti baru ada besok = the replacement flight isn't there until tomorrow.

target: Kami ketinggalan pesawat karena macet di jalan tol.
english: We missed the plane because of a traffic jam on the toll road.
tip: English says you missed the plane; Indonesian says the plane left you behind: ketinggalan pesawat = got left behind by the plane.

target: Permisi, AC di kamar kami rusak sejak tadi malam.
english: Excuse me, the AC in our room has been broken since last night.
tip: AC is said a-se; rusak = broken: AC-nya rusak = the AC is broken.

target: Kamar sebelah berisik sekali sampai kami tidak bisa tidur.
english: The room next door is so noisy that we can't sleep.
tip: sampai usually means until, but after a description it means so much that: berisik sekali sampai kami tidak bisa tidur = so noisy we couldn't sleep.

target: Toilet di kamar kami mampet sejak siang tadi.
english: The toilet in our room has been clogged since midday.
tip: mampet = clogged, the everyday word; tersumbat is what a plumber's report says.

target: Air di kamar mandi keluarnya kecil sekali pagi ini.
english: The water in the bathroom is only coming out in a trickle this morning.
tip: keluarnya kecil = its flow is weak: -nya turns keluar (come out) into 'the coming-out'.

target: Kami sudah menelepon dua kali, tapi belum ada yang datang.
english: We have already called twice, but no one has come yet.
tip: belum = not yet, and it's the negative for anything still pending: belum ada yang datang = no one has come yet. Tidak would state it flatly, as if no one will.

target: Masalah air panasnya selesai setelah teknisi datang.
english: The hot water problem was resolved after the technician came.
tip: -nya on a whole phrase marks it as the one already discussed: masalah air panasnya = that hot-water problem.

target: Boleh lihat SIM Anda sebelum motornya dibawa?
english: May I see your driving licence before the motorbike is taken?
tip: SIM = driving licence (Surat Izin Mengemudi); said sim.

target: Sewa seminggu lebih murah daripada sewa harian.
english: Renting for a week is cheaper than daily rental.
tip: Stick -an on a time word to get a 'per' word: hari – harian (daily), minggu – mingguan (weekly), bulan – bulanan (monthly). Sewa harian = daily rental.

target: Ayah menyewa mobil besar supaya seluruh keluarga muat.
english: Dad rented a big car so the whole family would fit.
tip: seluruh = the whole of one thing: seluruh keluarga = the whole family; semua keluarga = all the (separate) families.

target: Tiket pulang pergi lebih murah daripada dua tiket sekali jalan.
english: A round-trip ticket is cheaper than two one-way tickets.
tip: Pulang pergi is literally 'go-home go' – the trip home gets named first. Tiket pulang pergi = a round-trip ticket, often shortened to PP on booking sites.

target: Kapal ke pulau berangkat dua kali sehari dari pelabuhan.
english: The boat to the island departs twice a day from the harbor.
tip: The everyday way to say per is se- (one): dua kali sehari = twice a day, literally two times one-day.

target: Kami salah beli tanggal, tiketnya harus diubah di loket.
english: We bought the wrong date; the ticket has to be changed at the window.
tip: Salah slots before almost any verb to mean doing it wrong: salah beli = bought the wrong one, salah paham = misunderstood, salah sambung = dialed the wrong number.

target: Permisi, numpang tanya, stasiun kereta arah mana, ya?
english: Excuse me, may I ask, which way is the train station?
tip: Numpang tanya = set phrase to stop a stranger politely, like excuse me, may I ask.

target: Maaf, Pak, jalan ke pelabuhan lewat mana, ya?
english: Excuse me, sir, which way is the road to the harbor?
tip: Pak or Bu before a question keeps it polite: Maaf, Pak, ... = excuse me, sir.

target: Maaf sudah merepotkan, terima kasih atas bantuannya.
english: Sorry for the trouble, and thank you for your help.
tip: Maaf sudah merepotkan = sorry for the trouble — polite closer after someone helps.

target: Kalau boleh tahu, Bapak asalnya dari mana?
english: If I may ask, where are you from, sir?
tip: Kalau boleh tahu = if I may ask — softens personal questions.

target: Liburan ke sini sama keluarga atau sendiri, Mas?
english: Are you on holiday here with family or alone, sir?
tip: sama normally means same, but in everyday speech it also means with: sama keluarga = with family. Dengan is the formal version.

target: Kami ingin mengundang kamu ke acara syukuran rumah baru.
english: We would like to invite you to a housewarming celebration.
tip: Syukuran = a small thanksgiving do for good news; syukuran rumah baru = a housewarming.

target: Kamu mau datang ke ulang tahun anak saya hari Minggu?
english: Do you want to come to my child's birthday on Sunday?
tip: Datang ke + event or place = come to: datang ke ulang tahun = come to the birthday. The ke never drops.

target: Kamu jadi datang ke nikahan teman kantor besok?
english: Are you still coming to our coworker's wedding tomorrow?
tip: Jadi before a verb checks a plan still holds: Kamu jadi datang? = Are you still coming?

target: Dia mengajak kami makan malam di rumahnya minggu ini.
english: She invited us to have dinner at her house this week.
tip: Mengajak = casually ask someone along; mengundang = properly invite. Dia mengajak kami makan = asked us to eat.

target: Jangan lupa ajak suami kamu ke acara arisan nanti.
english: Don't forget to bring your husband to the arisan later.
tip: Arisan = a monthly savings-and-social gathering; members pool money and one takes the pot.

target: Datang saja langsung, tidak perlu bawa apa-apa.
english: Just come right over; no need to bring anything.
tip: After a negative, apa-apa = anything: tidak perlu bawa apa-apa = no need to bring anything.

target: Nikahan sepupu saya bulan depan di gedung dekat alun-alun.
english: My cousin's wedding is next month at a hall near the town square.
tip: Nikahan is the everyday word for a wedding; pernikahan is the formal one on invitations.
